guides.title: Ocean swimming
guides.intro: Choose the setting, check the conditions and plan both entry and exit. A location listing is a starting point for research, not a swim route or a conditions report.

sections.title: Start with local advice
sections.text: Choose a patrolled beach and swim between the red and yellow flags where possible. Read the signs and ask a lifesaver or lifeguard about the conditions before entering.

sections.title: Check the sea on the day
sections.text: Check the official marine forecast and warnings before leaving and again at the beach. Wind, waves and tide can change your entry and exit; a clear-water photo may be from a very different day.

sections.title: Plan an exit before a distance
sections.text: Identify where you will get in, get out and leave the water early if conditions change. Do not treat a straight line on the depth map as an established ocean-swimming course.

sections.title: Swim with support
sections.text: Arrange company and let someone know your plan. Choose conditions within your experience; if unsure, seek advice from the local lifesaving service or an organised ocean-swimming group.

sections.title: Understand rips and exposure
sections.text: Learn rip-current recognition and response from Surf Life Saving. A beach can have hazards even when the surface looks inviting; do not infer protection from a bay name or historical photograph.

sections.title: Use this guide’s location facts
sections.text: Look for documented entry and exit, setting, exposure and facilities. “Unknown” means the source has not established that fact. Northern waters may have additional local hazards and restrictions: follow the relevant parks and lifesaving advice.

guides.title: Freediving
guides.intro: Use the map to understand reference depth and access, then plan the actual dive with suitable training, a trained buddy and current local advice.

sections.title: Read the depth reference
sections.text: A contour labels a surveyed reference depth. It is not today’s water depth: tides, swell, the source datum and survey age matter. Point depths and profiles appear only where a numeric survey grid is published.

sections.title: Read the starting point
sections.text: The distance may start at a monitoring point, gazetted place reference, documented access location or mapped 0 m contour. Check the label. A beach-centre point may be offshore and is not your entry point.

sections.title: Use trained buddy procedures
sections.text: Do not freedive alone. Learn and practise appropriate buddy supervision and rescue procedures with a qualified instructor. DAN discusses the importance of one-up-one-down practice and the limits of supervision as complexity increases.

sections.title: Avoid performance targets from a map
sections.text: A nearby 10 m contour is not a recommendation to dive to 10 m. Stay within your training and experience, and choose a site where entry, observation and exit can be managed.

sections.title: Breathing and training
sections.text: Do not hyperventilate before breath-hold diving. Learn preparation, recovery and rescue through formal instruction rather than using this directory as a training programme.

sections.title: Check access and traffic
sections.text: Inspect entry and exit, current conditions, visibility and boat traffic. Consider the local requirements for dive flags and floats. A ruler line can cross rocks, channels or restricted water and is not a checked route.

guides.title: Spearfishing
guides.intro: Research the exact water, the method and the species before planning a trip. This directory does not issue permission to fish.

sections.title: Check the jurisdiction first
sections.text: Use the state or territory rules and the applicable marine-park zoning for the water you intend to enter. A tourism region can cross a legal boundary; Commonwealth and state or territory requirements may both be relevant.

sections.title: Check more than the beach name
sections.text: Confirm current licences, spearfishing closures, gear restrictions, protected species, size and bag limits, and seasonal rules. A missing restriction in this directory means “not established”, not “allowed”.

sections.title: Check the exact boundaries
sections.text: Follow the authority’s current closure and zoning maps. The beach reference point and the nearest depth contour can lie on different sides of a boundary.

sections.title: Plan the dive with your buddy
sections.text: Spearfishing adds tasks to breath-hold diving. Keep buddy procedures and rescue skills within your training and experience; reading habitat or depth information does not assess dive safety.

sections.title: Separate equipment from other water users
sections.text: Follow the authority’s equipment and public-area guidance. VFA’s guidance includes unloading a speargun before taking it out of the water; check your own jurisdiction’s requirements.

sections.title: Use the site facts as research
sections.text: Documented entry, habitat and reference depths help you identify questions to check. Known restrictions exclude a location from spearfishing suggestions here. Other suggestions remain research leads, with permission unconfirmed.
